metadata.methods_description: EEG data were acquired using g.USBamp hardware (g.tec) at a sampling rate of 256 Hz from 32 channels arranged in a standard 1020 montage. The experimental paradigm employed a 9x8 character grid with visual presentation of target and non-target stimuli. Data were collected across 2 sessions per subject using a calibration-then-test cross-validation approach with within-subject evaluation. Line frequency was 60 Hz.

citation_details.title: Limits of Trial-Adaptive Neural–Language Fusion Across Large Language Models in P300 Brain–Computer Interfaces
citation_details.author: Alon Gorenshtein, Mahmud Omar, Eric Jia, Yosef Adiniaev, Oved Daniel, Jonathan B. Kruskal, Muneeb Ahmed, Olga Rachel Brook, Eyal Klang, Yiftach Barash
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Objective Published P300-speller fusion schemes fix prior trust regardless of trial reliability; we tested whether a reliability estimate improves on it. Methods We reanalyzed 3,373 archived P300-speller selections from 47 people with ALS (BigP3BCI). A fair, matched-search-space comparison, tuning both a fixed weight and an adaptive policy out-of-fold, was evaluated across 22 evaluable language-model priors up to 46.7B parameters. Two representative priors, GPT-2 and a classical 5-gram, additionally received detailed naive and mechanistic analyses. Results No prior’s 95% CI favored adaptive fusion under the fair comparison, despite unexploited oracle headroom at every scale. Under GPT-2, the naive comparison was significantly worse for adaptive fusion; both anchors converged to a degenerate or near-degenerate fair-comparison solution. citation_details.title: Quantifying Large Language Model Influence in Brain Computer Interface Communication for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
citation_details.author: Alon Gorenshtein, Mahmud Omar, Eric Jia, Yosef Adiniaev, Oved Daniel, Jonathan B. Kruskal, Muneeb Ahmed, Olga Rachel Brook, Yiftach Barash, Eyal Klang
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Large language models are integrated into brain-computer interfaces for communication, but accuracy does not show whether an emitted character depended on neural evidence or on the language-model prior. We retrospectively re-decoded 3,373 P300-speller selections from 47 people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, reconstructing a neural posterior and combining it with 25 language priors ranging from 5-grams to 46.7-billion-parameter models. Under held-out, per-source calibration and equal fusion weighting, the prior accounted for a participant-weighted mean 8.6% of posterior displacement (median across selections, 2.9%); the corresponding neural contribution fraction was 0.914 (95% CI, 0.896-0.934).
